title: Choose pod-god's visual world
question: Keep Session Tape Log, take a challenger, or ask for a fresh roll.

options.label: Session Tape Log
options.lineage: field recorder cases, tape logs, and cue sheets
options.thesis: The assistant is the producer's running session log; every approved artifact becomes a labeled take.
options.viewport: A wide conversation ledger leads while a compact production rail shows the next stage, active take, and one primary action.
options.risk: Literal tape styling could become nostalgic unless every label carries real workflow state.

options.label: Broadcast Teletext
options.thesis: The workflow is a live broadcast index whose numbered pages expose one production state at a time.
options.case: Strong broadcast recognition, but page-number navigation is less natural than a conversation-led flow.
options.viewport: Chat occupies the live page while a three-digit index jumps to scripts, voices, renders, and playback.
options.risk: The rigid character grid can reduce scanning comfort and make long scripts feel cramped.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Production artifacts become a digital specimen where scale, density, and pixel texture reveal importance.
options.case: Sharpens the existing pixel identity, but reads more software studio than podcast studio.
options.viewport: A poster-scale prompt anchors the page with chat and production modules arranged as dense specimen blocks.
options.risk: Display typography can overpower the actual conversation and editing tasks.

options.label: Production Route Catalog
options.lineage: numbered convention catalogs and hand-marked route maps
options.thesis: Episodes are catalog entries and the production plan is a route the creator marks through them.
options.case: Maps progress beautifully, but its browse-first grid competes with chat as the product's center.
options.viewport: A conversation column marks a path through an episode grid, with the current production stop enlarged beside it.
options.risk: The catalog metaphor can make sequential creation feel like asset browsing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar AI workspace with chat beside a conventional production dashboard, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A chat column leads, with a step navigator and contextual production form beside it.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but visually interchangeable with other AI workflow products.
